history.origins: Developed in 19th century from Austrian Zwanzigerrufen. Known as Paskievics (after Russian commander Paskevich); 42-card pack, call XX for partner; favoured by Hungarian establishment; discouraged in communist era, interest reviving.
timeline: Modern Era: Revival of interest in Hungary

setup.players: Four active players per hand; five may participate with the dealer sitting out each hand. Partnerships change each hand and are determined by the high bidder calling a tarokk, usually the XX.
setup.dealing: Dealer places 6 face-down as talon; then 5 cards to each player, then 4 each (9 per player). After auction, declarer and others exchange with talon and discard to 9.

scoring.description: Card points in tricks (kings 5, queens 4, riders 3, jacks 2, tens/aces 1; honours 5 each, other tarokks 1). Total 94. Declarer's side needs at least 48 to win game. Bonuses for all honours, all kings, pagát ultimo, catching XXI with skíz; announced bonuses double; kontra doubles stake.
scoring.winCondition: Declarer's team wins the hand by taking at least 48 of 94 card points; game and bonus payments settled after each hand.
